facts.fact: The StackAdapt blog post on live sports and events advertising was published on August 10, 2020.
The article presents five best practices for running ads in live sports and events, as stated by SpotX's Ben Elliott.
facts.quote: #### 5. Be device agnostic with your campaigns.

facts.fact: The article says advertisers should be aware of three challenges in live sports and events advertising: forecasting, advanced planning, and underdelivery.
facts.quote: Advertisers should be aware of these 3 things:

facts.fact: According to SpotX, CTV is a device that enables an end user to stream content through their television, such as a Smart TV or a streaming stick or gaming console.
facts.quote: a device that enables an end user to stream content through their television

facts.fact: According to SpotX, OTT is broadcast-quality content streamed across all devices.
facts.quote: broadcast-quality content streamed across all devices

facts.fact: SpotX states that total opportunities for live sports forecasting equal the number of viewers multiplied by the number of ad breaks.
facts.quote: total opportunities is the number of viewers multiplied by the number of ad breaks

facts.fact: SpotX says it can implement dayparting at the deal ID level, so DSPs and advertisers do not need to make manual hourly adjustments around event times.
facts.quote: SpotX has the ability to implement dayparting at the deal ID level

facts.fact: The article's example of an event package contrasts buying the NFL season with buying week 5 of the Denver Broncos, recommending the season-level package to help meet impression goals.
facts.quote: Buying by event packages means buying the NFL season vs. week 5 of the Denver Broncos.

facts.fact: The article recommends sending creatives to SpotX ahead of a live event so the publisher can approve and upload them, noting approval is easier in the days before the event than the night before or day of.
facts.quote: It’s easier to get the creative approval process locked in during the days leading up to the event vs. the night before or day of.
